solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: African country’s limited by class system rigidly applied (9)

indicators.note: the country is hemmed in by the class, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a form is a school class
MALI'S, the West African state plus its 's

explanation.surface: A comment on a rigid class system limiting an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'country's' is used as letters, not grammar, so the country goes in with its S attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalism is strict adherence to prescribed forms, a system applied rigidly.

clue.text: Healthier, having swallowed right bit of food (7)

indicators.note: the healthier word takes the letter inside it

explanation.surface: Someone getting healthier despite having swallowed a morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of food' sounds like a morsel being swallowed, but it is the definition, and the swallowing is done by the healthier word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fritter is a small piece of battered fried food.

clue.text: A revolutionary agent here (3)

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: 'a' as in '£5 a head' means per

explanation.surface: Announcing that a revolutionary agent is present.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'A' as PER, as in 'twice a day'; turned round it is REP.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep, short for representative, is a sales agent.

clue.text: Article penned by mature editor is greatly praised (8)

indicators.note: the article is enclosed, as in a pen, by the other letters

explanation.surface: A news item: an article by a mature editor has won high praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature editor' reads as a veteran journalist, but the two words are separate pieces, and the article slips in near the end of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to praise excessively, so adulated is greatly praised.

clue.text: River in which to find religious types (hard to miss) (5)

indicators.note: to miss something is to leave it out, so the religious types go without their H

blocks.note: H = hard, as on pencils; this is removed

explanation.surface: A river on whose banks one finds religious people who are hard to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an aside about how conspicuous the worshippers are; it is the instruction to remove H from HINDUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming by class: the Indus is one particular river, flowing from Tibet through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Festival diagrams organised, with involvement of rector initially (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order
the extra letter is brought into the mix
take the first letter of rector

explanation.surface: Planning a festival: the diagrams are organised with the rector's help.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra R is needed because DIAGRAMS has only one R and MARDI GRAS has two.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is a carnival festival.

clue.text: Bill enters inn, rolling over in northern town (5)

indicators.note: the bill goes into the inn
the inn is turned back to front

blocks.note: a pub is an inn; reversed it is BUP

explanation.surface: A bill arrives at a pub as the drinkers roll over in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacup is a small town in Lancashire, in northern England. AC goes inside BUP after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a town in Rossendale, Lancashire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Description of sea food, cooked then cold (6)

blocks.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal pan, a British-Indian dish

explanation.surface: A description of seafood, cooked and then served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea food' reads as seafood, but 'Description of sea' is the definition. 'Cooked' looks like an anagram signal; here it just describes the balti.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing by name: Baltic is what the sea between Scandinavia and the Baltic states is called.

clue.text: Officer is in charge of venomous types (11)

blocks.note: a copper is a police officer
to head something is to lead it

explanation.surface: An officer taking charge of dangerous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venomous types' sounds like nasty people; it means snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Copperheads are venomous North American snakes.

clue.text: Happy prisoner’s first to get let out (7)

indicators.note: take only the first letter of prisoner

blocks.note: to let out a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: A prisoner is happy to be let out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' suggests release from prison; it means rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be pleased with something is to be happy about it.

clue.text: Ezra’s personal claim comes with “Shut up!” (7)

blocks.note: the American poet Ezra Pound stating who he is, in the first person with his surname
shut up as a verb: to confine, as stray animals or seized goods are

explanation.surface: The poet Ezra Pound claims something and is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: What Ezra Pound would say of himself is I'M POUND, run together as one word. 'Shut up!' is not a rude command but the verb to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound is to shut up or confine, as a pound holds strays.

clue.text: She’s pale, really going backwards — this being evident? (7)

definitions.text: She’s pale, really going backwards — this being evident?

indicators.note: the letters are read right to left
the answer is on view in the clue's words

explanation.surface: A patient's pallor shows that she is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pale patient going backwards is having a relapse, and the word lies backwards in her description.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a going back into illness, which pallor would make evident.

clue.text: Time in the morning old man appears in US city (5)

explanation.surface: An old man shows up in an American city one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appears in' reads as a container instruction; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Tampa, on Florida's Gulf coast, is one American city.

clue.text: Plot devised by Greek character in mother country (11)

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes inside the rest

explanation.surface: A plot hatched by a Greek in his mother country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: machination, usually plural, means a crafty scheme or intrigue.

clue.text: Bone, one attached to head, showing glossy quality (9)

blocks.note: a ness is a headland; 'attached to' just places it after

explanation.surface: Anatomy: a bone attached to the head, with a shiny look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not the one on your shoulders but a headland, NESS, as in place names like Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: The abstract noun from shiny: a glossy surface has exactly that lustre.

clue.text: Noise always reveals criminal (9)

explanation.surface: Constant noise gives a criminal away.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic contraction of ever, a common crossword piece for 'always'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: someone who runs a fraudulent or extortionate business is one kind of criminal.

clue.text: See person so nobly seated? (9)

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, so its person is the bishop, not someone you look at
a new bishop is installed on the cathedral throne with ceremony

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at someone sitting grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a bishop's diocese: a see person is a bishop, who is formally seated on a throne when taking office.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's installation in the cathedral of the see is a ceremonial seating on the throne, which is as noble as seating gets.

clue.text: The female driver’s first in ditch (4)

indicators.note: take only the first letter of driver

explanation.surface: A woman driver ends up in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a roadside trench for the car; it is the verb meaning get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to cast off a skin or a burden is to get rid of, ditch, it.

clue.text: Belt tune out — an aid to digestion! (5,3)

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Singing loudly after a meal to help it go down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' reads as a verb for singing loudly, which hides that it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel nut, the areca nut, is chewed in Asia partly as a digestive after meals.

clue.text: A bit firm, having got implanted? (4)

explanation.surface: A company has had a small implant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' is a coin, as in a threepenny bit, an old British coin; it is not 'a little'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British sense: bit was long used for a small piece of money, as in the old threepenny bit.

clue.text: A hundred presents in boxes (7)

explanation.surface: A hundred gifts packed in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' looks like the noun, gifts; it is the verb, offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coffers are chests for money and valuables, so strong boxes.

clue.text: Somehow recast set into 4D figure (9)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Somehow reshaping a set into a four-dimensional shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recast' is itself an anagram-flavoured word, but here it is fodder; the instruction is the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tesseract is the four-dimensional analogue of a cube.

clue.text: Lever altered, readjusted (7)

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: A lever has been altered and then readjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' looks like the anagram signal next to 'Lever', but LEVER cannot give seven letters; ALTERED is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever, as on a sewing machine.

clue.text: Pursuit around India in carriage (6)

indicators.note: the chase goes round the letter

blocks.note: I = India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A chase around India in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: India is I from the NATO phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo… India), a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Like wren given food, eating at this place (9)

indicators.note: the fed letters take the place words inside them

explanation.surface: A wren is given food and eats it here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At this place' is taken word by word: AT stays as it is and 'this place' is HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the wren is a bird, and having feathers is what marks birds out.

clue.text: After protest see bishop leaving service (5)

indicators.note: the bishop comes after the protest

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: After a protest, a bishop is seen quitting the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' sounds like a church service beside 'bishop'; it is military service, and demob is British slang for release from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob, short for demobilisation, is leaving the armed services.

clue.text: Woman being different, I gathered (5)

indicators.note: the I is gathered into the other word

explanation.surface: A woman who is different, or so I gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' reads as 'I understand'; in fact ELSE has gathered I.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Elsie, a pet form of Elizabeth, is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Priest coming to holy mount, cutting bit of speech short (7)

blocks.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel
Sion (Zion), the holy hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A priest arrives at a holy mountain and cuts his sermon short.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is crosswordland's standard priest, from the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the cutting short of a sound or syllable in speech, as in 'don't'.

clue.text: Fellow gets top award for vegetable (7)

explanation.surface: A man wins first prize for his vegetable at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangold, or mangel-wurzel, is a large beet grown for cattle feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangold is a root vegetable, a variety of beet.

clue.text: Getting up, little brother to turn round (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A little brother climbing up to turn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is the noun, a sphere, not the direction in 'turn round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense of round: a sphere or globe is a round thing.

clue.text: Minor damage from fire one’s left to go out (5)

indicators.note: something that goes out leaves the room, so the left letter departs from the word for one

explanation.surface: A fire mostly burned out, leaving a little damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left to go out' looks like a fire allowed to die; it tells you L leaves SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to scorch only the surface is the lightest damage fire can do.

clue.text: Dubious socialite brought before a board (9)

indicators.note: the socialite is placed in front

blocks.note: a deb, debutante, is a young society woman

explanation.surface: A shady socialite is brought before the board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee; it is a table, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something debatable is open to doubt, dubious.
